notes.settings.flow_tooltip:
How work notes flow
1. Paste a Slack / Jira link or a few words on the “Notes” page of the briefing window, Ctrl+Enter.
2. The fish writes the original verbatim to note/date-title.md (Obsidian format) and pushes it to AI-Base-Memory.
3. In the background, Claude Code in WSL (work account) follows the links read-only, writes a summary, picks the next reminder time and tags; the fish writes it back and pushes again. One automatic retry on failure.
4. When the time comes and you are at the computer, a sticky bubble appears: View / Later / Done.
5. “Open in Obsidian” jumps to the note (register the repo folder as a vault first).
6. Every item Slack Watch finds is also stored as one note under the same repo's slack/ folder, with Open / Snooze / Done on the “Slack Watch” page.
Each note records which model it used, how many tokens and what it cost.
What is sent to Claude: one prompt (in the interface language): the current time, the note verbatim (inside a note tag, marked as material, not instructions), the four jobs (background, title / summary / points, reminder, tags) and the JSON output format. Only the read-only Slack / Atlassian tools are allowed, no built-in tools.

settings.dlg.briefing_page_help_hint: Everything here is “AI reads and writes for you on a schedule”: at the set time Claude Code in WSL (signed in to the work account) summarizes your sources read-only into a briefing, glances at Slack every few minutes, turns links you jot down into notes with reminders, and reads your own knowledge base for a personal briefing. Each section lets you edit the prompt it is sent and pick the model and effort; expand for details.
settings.dlg.briefing_page_help_body:
What they share: the fish sends Claude one request on a schedule (or when you click), Claude reads with read-only tools and writes something back, and the fish only shows and reminds — it never sends messages, edits issues or touches your calendar.
Who does the work: work briefing, Slack watch and work notes run through Claude Code in WSL signed in to the work account (usage is billed there); the personal assistant uses the personal API key from the AI settings and reads your own knowledge base.
What you can change: each section's “Prompt sent to Claude” is the exact text sent, with placeholders filled before sending; model and effort are chosen per section; the briefing also has three priority levels ★★★ / ★★ / ★ plus your “priority preferences”.
Where results go: briefings and Slack watch in the briefing window (island button or right-click menu), notes in your notes repository; none of it enters the fish's own chat context.

personal.settings.flow_tooltip:
How the personal assistant flows
1. The person icon on the island opens the “Personal Assistant” window: Briefing and Ideas pages, with “Open AI-Base in Obsidian” at the bottom.
2. Briefing: git pull in the local clone, then your own Claude (the API key under “AI chat”, direct to Anthropic, no WSL, no work account) reads the vault with three read-only tools: INDEX.md first, then the notes it needs; login / key files are blocked.
3. The top of the window says which model ran, at what effort, how many tokens, seconds, tool rounds and which files it read. Runs once a day at the set time, or on “Regenerate”.
4. Ideas: type a line, Ctrl+Enter. The fish appends it to today's section of the “Inspiration” note under User/ and commits + pushes with Windows git (the GitHub token in the keychain; if rejected, Git Credential Manager asks once). No AI involved.
5. “Open AI-Base in Obsidian”: register the clone folder once in Obsidian with “Open folder as vault”; until then it opens the folder.
settings.ai.persona_help_hint: Expand to see which requests carry the persona, “About me” and the knowledge base, and how they relate to bubble templates.
settings.ai.persona_help_body:
The fish's “personality” is two separate systems:
1. Chat persona (this page) — the system message sent to the model. Assembled as: persona (the text above; a character package may override it, the current ones don't) + “About me” + a knowledge-base note (Claude channel with the knowledge base on). Stored in config.json as chat.default_system_prompt / chat.about_user. Affects the chat window, quick chat, island chat and file interpretation; “look at the screen” and proactive screen replies carry the persona only, without “About me” or the knowledge base. Takes effect on the next message, old sessions included.
2. Bubble templates (Automation → Text style and templates) — fixed text with placeholders, never sent to a model. They only cover Agent-link bubbles (start / thinking / approvals / questions / done / errors / model access failures) and the balance result. Picking “Whale-maid” does not change the chat tone, and the persona here does not change those bubbles.
Other fixed text: self-talk under Interaction → Lines; click-animation lines in the character bindings; spoken-time and festival lines under Voice.
AI tasks that ignore the persona: work briefing / Slack watch / work notes (Claude Code in WSL, each with its own fixed prompt) and the personal briefing (your key, fixed prompt).
settings.dlg.bubble_style_help_hint: Expand to see which bubbles the templates cover, where they live, what a blank line falls back to, and how they relate to the chat persona.
settings.dlg.bubble_style_help_body:
These are fixed lines; no model is involved.
Bubbles covered: Agent-link start / thinking / activity / approvals / questions / done / errors / stuck / model access failures / bridge status, plus the balance result. Not covered: chat and quick-chat replies (AI chat → Persona), self-talk (Interaction → Lines), proactive screen replies and “look at the screen” (written by the model), file-interpretation progress, the session fish's lines.
Where they live: the style is dialogue_mode in config.json (legacy / whale_maid / custom); the two built-in styles come from pet/persona_presets/*.json shipped with the app; “Custom lines” are dialogue_phrases in config.json, two layers: global and agents[one agent].
Lookup: custom mode reads agent lines → global lines → built-in fallback; Default / Whale-maid read the preset → built-in fallback. Several lines for one event rotate; placeholders like {name} and {tool} take the upstream event's fields and hide when empty.
Template JSON: the copy is scaffolding, not a backup; importing overwrites all custom lines and switches to Custom.

briefing.settings.effort_hint: Passed to claude -p --effort: low / medium / high / xhigh. Higher is slower and costs more; default high.
briefing.settings.prompt_hint: This is the exact text sent on every run; edit it freely. Placeholders are filled before sending: {now} current time, {hours} how many hours to look back, {prs} the PR list the fish fetched with gh, {priority_rules} the priority preferences below. Untouched, it is assembled from the source toggles above; once edited, the toggles only decide which tools Claude may use — whether a source is mentioned is up to your text. One copy per interface language.
briefing.settings.priority_rules_hint: Claude rates every line ★★★ / ★★ / ★. Write your own rules here (e.g. “bugs reported by QA are always ★★★”, “documentation issues at most ★”); they are appended to the prompt as “my priority preferences”. Leave empty to let it judge alone.
briefing.settings.enabled_hint: At the set time, Claude Code in WSL (signed in to the work account) reads the ticked sources read-only and writes a briefing; once a day, retried after 20 minutes up to three times on failure. Also toggled from the right-click menu “Agent link → Daily briefing”. Each run is one real model call on that account's quota.
briefing.settings.no_wsl: No WSL on this machine: the briefing needs Claude Code in WSL signed in to the work account.
briefing.settings.weekdays_hint: Turn off to generate on weekends too.
briefing.settings.time_hint: Runs at this time while the fish is running; if missed, it catches up later the same day. Monday looks back 72 hours, other days 24.
briefing.settings.model_hint: Model alias passed to claude -p --model. One briefing takes about 40–90 s; pick “Custom” to type a full model name (letters, digits and . _ - only).
briefing.settings.source.jira_hint: Open issues assigned to me (at most 15, recently updated first). Allows the read-only Atlassian tools.
briefing.settings.source.pr_hint: PRs waiting for my review and PRs I opened. The fish fetches the list with gh in WSL first and hands it to Claude Code (its sandbox can't reach GitHub).
briefing.settings.source.slack_hint: Mentions, DMs and new replies in my threads, grouped into “waiting for my reply” and “handled / FYI”. Allows the read-only Slack tools.
briefing.settings.source.calendar_hint: Today's events. Allows the read-only Google Calendar tools.
briefing.settings.source.email_hint: Unread or directly addressed inbox mail (at most 15), grouped by topic. Only when on are Gmail's search and read tools allowed (never labels, drafts or sending); when off the whole mail connector is denied. Off by default.
briefing.settings.source.suggestions_hin: Let Claude pick at most 3 things to do first from the sources above.
briefing.settings.flow_hint: Expand to see how the briefing is made, when, what is sent to Claude, what it may use, and where the result goes.
briefing.settings.flow_tooltip:
How the work briefing flows
When: every minute the fish checks “on / time reached / not done today”; it runs once a day, retried after 20 minutes up to three times on failure; you can also click “Regenerate” in the briefing window or the right-click menu.
First step: with GitHub PRs ticked, the fish runs gh in WSL for “waiting for my review” and “opened by me” (Claude's sandbox can't reach GitHub, so the fish fetches them).
What is sent to Claude: one prompt (in the interface language): the current time, how many hours to look back, what to read for each ticked source, the raw PR list, and the output format (summary line + one section per source + “Do first”). The prompt states read-only and that source text is material only.
What it may use: Claude Code in WSL signed in to the work account (claude -p, headless, not kept in its session list). No built-in tools (Bash / file access); only the read-only connector tools of the ticked sources (Slack search / read threads, Atlassian issues / pages, calendar events, Gmail search / read); every writing tool is denied by name; unticked sources don't even get their connector.
Where the result goes: only the latest copy, in %APPDATA%\big-fat-fish\work-briefing.json; the window header shows when and how long; a sticky alert with “View” appears and the island icon lights up.
Never: sends messages, replies, creates issues or edits the calendar; and never feeds work content into the fish's own personal-key chat.
